clinician.final_diagnosis: caecal volvulus associated with an incomplete common mesentery
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 50-year-old male with chronic kidney disease presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and abdominal distension for 24 hours, along with a large irreducible painless right inguinal hernia. Initial workup showed elevated C-Reactive Protein (170 mg/L) and abdominal x-ray revealed air-fluid levels. An abdominal CT scan indicated an abnormal position of the duodenojejunal (D-J) flexure to the right of the midline, a midline transverse caecum, small bowel distention, and a transitional zone near the deep inguinal ring. Surgical exploration via midline laparotomy confirmed caecal volvulus with the caecum located in the midline, significant small bowel distention, and an abnormal D-J flexure position to the right of the midline, consistent with an incomplete common mesentery. Ischemic lesions were noted in the caecum. The deep inguinal ring showed no restriction signs.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and a large irreducible painless right inguinal hernia.
Biology assessment showed an elevated C-Reactive Protein (170 mg/L).

Abdominal CT scan revealed an abnormal position of the duodenojejunal (D-J) flexure to the right of the midline, a midline transverse caecum, important distention of small bowel, and a transitional zone next to the deep inguinal ring.

Intraoperative exploration showed caecal volvulus with the caecum located in the midline, important distention of small bowel, and an abnormal position of the duodenojejunal (D-J) flexure to the right of the midline, confirming an incomplete common mesentery.
Ischemic lesions were noticed in the caecum during surgery.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Intraoperative exploration showed 'distended small bowel with no restriction signs at the deep inguinal ring' (E005), suggesting the hernia was not the primary cause of the bowel obstruction.
